title: Ledger migration phase 1: backfill legacy ledger rows into v2
body:
Backfill all historical ledger rows from the legacy table into ledger_v2. Runs in batches of 50k with checkpointing so it can be resumed. Success criteria: row counts match the legacy ledger and a sampled diff shows zero drift on amount, currency and posted_at.

Result: 41,204,882 rows backfilled in 3h44m over the weekend of 8/1. Two count verifications, both matched. Zero drift.

title: Ledger migration phase 2: dual-write to ledger_v2 behind a flag
body:
Write every ledger entry to both v1 and v2 behind flag ledger_v2_dual_write. Ramp 5% -> 25% -> 100%. v1 stays authoritative for the whole phase. Rollback is flipping the flag off; no data has to be undone because v2 is not read by anything yet.

Shadow read comparison runs alongside the ramp and diffs v1 against v2 on every read path.

title: Cut internal reporting reads over to ledger v2
body:
Once dual-write has been at 100% for 48h with a clean shadow comparison, move the internal reporting read path to ledger_v2. Merchant-facing payout views stay on v1 until phase 3.

Shadow comparison before cutover: 8.4m rows, 3 mismatches, all trailing-zero formatting on refund amounts (see NW-108). Judged non-blocking for internal reporting.

title: Nightly reconciliation job never reaches the dead letter cutoff
body:
The nightly reconciliation job retries failed batches forever instead of dead-lettering after 5 attempts. Root cause: the retry counter lives in memory on the job runner and resets whenever the scheduler reschedules the job, so it never reaches the cutoff.

Fix: persist retry_count on the job record and increment transactionally. Added a regression test that fails against the old behavior.

Delegated to John by Maya on 8/4 while Maya was on the ledger migration.

title: Q3 capacity estimate for payments (phase 3 + webhook hardening)
body:
Sam needs a rough eng-days estimate for Q3 payments work to feed the planning doc: ledger migration phase 3, webhook hardening follow-ups, and the reconciliation backlog. Rough is fine, ranges are fine.

Asked in DM on 8/7. No response yet.

title: Checkout redesign: address form and payment step
body:
Redesign of the checkout flow: new address form, new payment step, storybook coverage for both. PR #812.

Review from Maya left 14 comments, almost all on the address form, which was a set of booleans standing in for a state machine. Rewritten as an explicit state machine before merge. Merged 8/7, rolled out to 10% on 8/10 and 50% on 8/12.

title: Flaky test: test_settlement_batch_ordering fails intermittently on main
body:
test_settlement_batch_ordering has failed on main at least six times in two weeks, blocking unrelated PRs. Suspected ordering dependence on the shared batch fixture rather than a real settlement bug.

Confirmed: the batch fixture yields in dict insertion order and one test mutates the fixture in place, so ordering depends on which test ran first. Fix: fixture returns an explicitly ordered copy, mutating test deep-copies.

Delegated to John by Maya on 8/6, timeboxed to one day.

title: Refund amounts differ in trailing-zero formatting between ledger v1 and v2
body:
Shadow read comparison across 8.4m rows surfaced 3 mismatches, all on refunds: v1 stores 12.50 as "12.5" and v2 normalizes to "12.50". Values are numerically equal but the merchant-facing string differs, so this must be resolved before payouts move to v2 in phase 3.

Small, but merchant visible. Currently unowned.

title: Settlement webhook hardening: timestamp check, replay window, streaming verify
body:
Harden the inbound settlement webhook path.

- verify a signing timestamp header and reject anything outside a 5 minute tolerance
- track delivery ids in a replay window so a replayed payload is a no-op
- verify the signature over a streamed body instead of buffering the whole request
- raise the gateway request body limit (see NW-116)
- alert on gateway 5xx rate (see NW-110)

All five landed. Error rate on the settlement webhook is 0.02% over the last 24h.

title: Add alert on gateway 5xx rate
body:
Action item from the 8/11 settlement webhook incident. The gateway returned 502 for 30 minutes before anyone noticed, because every alert we have is on application error rate and the application never saw the requests.

Add an alert on gateway 5xx rate over 1% for 2 minutes, routed to the payments on-call.

title: Write a staging credential rotation doc that is true
body:
The old staging credential rotation doc was deleted because it documented the wrong port and the wrong vault, and people were following it. Nothing replaced it. Currently the process is 'ask Priya'.

Write a real one: vault location, rotation cadence, who to ask when it expires mid-migration.

title: Accept both signing keys during webhook signature rotation overlap
body:
Priya rotates the settlement webhook signing keys on 8/12. The verifier must accept signatures from both the old and new key for a 7 day overlap window, then the old key is removed.

- load both keys from the secret store, try new first
- emit a metric tagged with which key verified so we can watch old-key traffic drain
- hard-fail after 8/19

Delegated to John by Maya on 8/10.

title: Ledger migration phase 3: move merchant payout reads to v2
body:
Final phase. Move the merchant-facing payout views off ledger v1 and onto v2, then decommission the dual-write.

Open questions from the design doc:
- two payout queries join against legacy_settlement_batch, which has no v2 equivalent
- NW-108 (refund formatting) is merchant visible and blocks this
- decommission order: stop dual-write, then drop v1 read helpers, then drop the table (not before Q4)

Design doc circulates Friday 8/14, kickoff the following Tuesday.

title: Merchants served a stale cached copy of the old checkout
body:
Support forwarded a screenshot of the pre-redesign checkout from a merchant on the 10% rollout. The HTML shell was cached with a one year max-age set back in June and never revalidated.

Fix: cache-control on the shell drops to no-cache with an ETag; hashed asset bundles keep the long max-age.

title: Postmortem: settlement webhook 502s, 2026-08-11
body:
Impact: 08:37-09:52 UTC, 14% of inbound settlement webhook deliveries returned 502 at the gateway. No data loss; deliveries retried within the 6h window and the queue drained fully by 10:20. Merchants saw gaps in their settlement dashboards for roughly 90 minutes.

Cause: the hardened verifier reads the raw request body to check the signature, which caused the gateway to buffer the full request. Batch settlement payloads exceed the 256kb gateway body buffer limit, so the gateway rejected them before the application saw them.

What went right: the ingress-vs-app distinction was made in 12 minutes, which stopped us rolling back John's unrelated dual-key verify deploy.

What went wrong: we had no alert on gateway 5xx. Priya noticed from a latency dashboard.

Action items: NW-116 (raise body limit, stream the verify), NW-110 (alert on gateway 5xx rate). Both owned by Maya.

title: Raise gateway request body limit to 2mb and stream the verify body
body:
Mitigation and permanent fix for the 8/11 settlement webhook 502s.

- gateway request body buffer limit 256kb -> 2mb
- signature verifier consumes the body as a stream and computes the HMAC incrementally instead of holding the full payload in memory
- added a test with a 1.4mb batch settlement payload, which is the largest we have seen in prod

Deployed 09:44 on 8/11. Error rate fell from 14% to 0.03% within four minutes.

title: Webhook p99 latency regression: 240ms to 610ms over ten days
body:
Prod webhook p99 drifted from 240ms to 610ms over ten days with no corresponding deploy. Suspected contention from the nightly reconciliation job retrying without a dead letter cutoff (NW-104).

Confirmed: after the NW-104 fix landed, p99 recovered to 380ms. Not all the way back to 240ms, but the trend reversed and the remaining gap is attributed to the dual-write volume from NW-102.
